channel.name: Explained From Within
channel.spine: A recurring miniature explorer reveals how familiar things work and how they are made by observing hidden physical processes from within.
channel.promise: How things work and how they are made, explained from within.
channel.audience: General-audience curious teens and adults; educational entertainment, not child-directed programming.
channel.description:
Explained From Within reveals how familiar things work and how they are made by following hidden processes from trigger to result.

Travel with a miniature Explorer through the human body, materials, manufacturing, and technology. Each long-form Micro-Journey uses cinematic 3D visualization to make invisible or inaccessible mechanisms understandable.

Explore:
• Inside Your Body — ordinary biological processes
• Inside Materials — how substances form and change
• Inside Manufacturing — how inputs become useful objects
• Inside Technology — what happens inside devices

The Explorer and capsule are fictional guides. Explanations are researched, and each episode identifies simplified scale, timing, color, or visibility.

Hidden processes, made visible.
channel.keywords: how things work, how things are made, scientific visualization, 3D process animation, process explained, inside the human body, material science explained, manufacturing process, how technology works, engineering animation, inside view, hidden processes, Explained From Within
channel.shared_brand_note: This is the same real YouTube channel/brand as sibling-repo's inside-the-process profile (handle already claimed, EP001 already live there under LTX-2.5). This LTX profile does not re-claim the handle or re-produce that episode; it is a parallel production path for future episodes on this channel.

positioning.scope: The body is one series, not the channel boundary. Every episode explains one hidden causal process with a familiar outside-world payoff.
exclusions: Generic factory walkthroughs without an inside perspective
AI-tool tutorials and profession-specific software advice
Unsupported manufacturing mechanisms presented as fact

cast.explorer_voice_mode_note: OWNER RULE 2026-10-29, after the EP001 04h pilot. The Explorer's lines are a voice heard over the helmet radio, never on-screen speech. Clip prompts must not say the Explorer 'speaks' or 'says', and must not mention the Explorer's mouth or lips. The Explorer holds still (or keeps watching), with the dark visor unchanged. Why: every clip that asked for the Explorer to speak (SC11, SC21, SC22, SC31) made the visor transparent and rendered a face, a different face in each clip, which breaks CHARACTER_BIBLE.md:7,13 (the silhouette, not a face, is the identity). Control's off-screen lines never did. Listening beats also drop mouth language.

render.generation_unit_note: One approved frame-0 still conditions exactly one 20-second clip, carrying one primary causal action with a readable initial state and a stable changed state (EPISODE_SPEC.md). A whole biological, industrial or chemical transformation normally spans several clips, bridged in post with continuous room tone.
render.clip_duration_note: Fixed 20s, matching every other channel in this repo (universal AGENTS.md rule) — not the 15s this channel used under its LTX profile. At 24fps this is 481 frames (1 + 8*60); the render app takes seconds and derives the frame count itself.
render.closing_beat_frames_note: Frames in each clip's final, speech-free BEAT:: (camera move + Acoustic environment). The contract default is 120 (5 s). RE-DERIVED 2026-10-29 at EP001's first 04h pilot, owner-approved: with a 120-frame tail all 9 pilots ended in a mean 5.4 s of silence (the owner: 'a few words short, clips remain silent in the end'), because speech fills exactly the dialogue-beat window. 72 frames (3 s) gives dialogue ~1-17 s. Grade [B] (measured, qa/ltx-pilot-qa.json open_question_findings).
render.spoken_word_band_note: RE-DERIVED 2026-10-29 at EP001's first 04h pilot, owner-approved: 38-42 (was 32-36). Measured on 9 real renders: every authorised word delivered cleanly (Muse Voice Transcribe similarity 0.91-1.0) at a pooled 2.46 words/s, speech filling exactly the dialogue-beat window, the two-speaker Explorer + Control split included. With a 72-frame closing beat the window is ~16 s, which holds ~39-43 words at that rate. Grade [B]. Previous note: Carried from signed-anyway's derived native-in-clip band (~140-145 wpm filling ~70% of a 20s clip), which the removed Cut Plane test profile exercised with one narrator (pipeline/research/LTX25_PROMPTING_RESEARCH.md §7). UNVERIFIED here specifically: this channel splits dialogue between an on-screen Explorer and an off-screen Control voice within the same clip, a pattern neither sibling channel's evidence covers. Grade [C] — re-derive at the first pilot batch, and check whether a two-speaker split needs a narrower band than a single continuous narrator.
render.style_echo: Photorealistic cinematic scientific visualization, restrained exploration-film aesthetic, controlled directional light with readable depth, practical ivory-and-orange explorer equipment with restrained cyan navigation accents, explicitly photoreal and not illustrated or cel-shaded
render.style_echo_note: Built from VISUAL_STYLE_CONTRACT.md's reference style string plus an explicit photoreal lock (this channel is not painterly like signed-anyway). This exact string closes every clip prompt and is what LTXV-D041 excludes when locating the final action beat — keep prompt and channel.json identical if it changes.
render.look_and_feel: Photorealistic cinematic scientific visualization with a restrained exploration-film aesthetic. Believable material texture, controlled directional light, clear subject separation and readable depth. Practical ivory-and-orange Explorer equipment with restrained cyan navigation accents. Biological tissue, industrial materials and technological structures each retain their own documented geometry and material character. A convincing render is an illustration, not a measurement or recording — document enhanced visibility, false color, changed scale, time compression and cutaways in the episode's visualization ledger rather than silently mixing scales. Inline this whole clause into every Muse Image image prompt and every LTX clip prompt's style anchor.
render.on_screen_text: No native on-screen text. VISUAL_STYLE_CONTRACT.md directs that labels and captions are added in post-production editing, never requested from the image or video model — a consistency choice, since a sourced figure must read identically across every mention. LTXV-D012 stands for every clip prompt on this channel.

science.uncertain_claims: Resolve before scripting, omit, or label uncertainty explicitly.
science.time_and_scale: Document time compression, magnification, enhanced visibility, false color, conceptual cutaways and any metaphor. Do not imply literal microscope or hidden-camera footage.
science.qualified_review: Escalate disputed, uncertain or health-actionable claims to an appropriately qualified reviewer. Basic descriptive mechanisms use source-based editorial verification within the existing review gates. Record review scope; do not claim clinician validation without it.

youtube.default_disclosure: AI-generated scientific visualization. The explorer and capsule are fictional storytelling devices. The process explanation is based on the sources below; scale, timing, color and visibility may be simplified. This is not real microscopic or factory footage.

thumbnail_system.source_policy: Use accepted episode scenes or approved stills only. Do not invent a process state in the thumbnail.
thumbnail_system.typography_policy: Composite text deterministically after image generation whenever possible.
thumbnail_system.exception_policy: A deviation requires a documented episode-specific reason in metadata/package.md and an owner decision before upload.
thumbnail_system.adopted: 2026-10-29, from the sibling profile (owner: channel-setup changes only)

hard_safety_floor: No real, identifiable person, company, brand, product or event depicted.
No generated footage presented, framed or captioned as real recorded, microscopic or hidden-camera footage.
No medical diagnosis, treatment advice, guaranteed outcome or product health claim.
Non-graphic biological imagery only; drama comes from discovery, not fabricated emergency or fear.
Synthetic media disclosed on every upload, in the description and the YouTube disclosure field.
Every central explanatory claim traced to a direct source; an unresolved central claim blocks release.
No real-world insignia on any character: no national flag, mission patch, shoulder patch, arm badge or chest emblem on the Explorer or the "you" figure.
Never show drinking alcohol or smoking on screen; research and narration about them are allowed.
